16: Khudkasht holds customary rights and pays by patta. Zamindar is a 10% commission collector (Vatan right), not owner; only the King owns. Hurry for money means auction (Ijaradari).
EIC gets the Diwani, keeps the Mughal chain under Muhammad Reza Khan. Patta ignored, rents soar, drought: Great Bengal Famine 1770 kills 50 lakh to 1 crore. Reza Khan jailed 1772-74 as scapegoat.
EIC bought goods with India's land revenue, so famine hit its income. Near bankrupt, it takes 1.4 million pounds at 4% from Parliament, which brings the Regulating Act 1773.

Warren Hastings 73-85 auctions each district to a Revenue Farmer under a European District Collector. Farmers squeeze ryots to recover bids; demand too high, peasants pay nothing, revenue does not improve.
Cornwallis 86-93 trusts English landlordism. Permanent Settlement 1793: Zamindar owner, LR fixed forever at 10/11 of 1789-90 (Rs 66 to Rs 60), Sunset Clause auctions defaulters.

Early auctions, then loyal Zamindars and certain revenue. But no investment, absentee owners, ryot a tenant at will with patta ignored. Wellesley 98-05 restores coercion (Regulation VII of 1799); courts clog.

Rent Act 1859: occupancy after 12 years, patta revived, no imprisonment; Zamindars evict at year 11. Indigo Revolt, Pabna follow. Ripon 80-84's commission leads to Bengal Tenancy Act 1885 under Dufferin 84-88.

Big Zamindars through Poligars fail in Madras. Read begins Ryotwari in Baramahal 1792; Thomas Munro convinces the Directors 1801, rules Madras 1820-27. Yeoman ideology: ryot owns, settled directly after field survey.
Gross-produce demand of 33% to 50% ruins ryots. Net produce: Pringle 1830 reaches 55%, Wingate Settlement 1835 fixes 30 years. Cotton boom of 1861-65 collapses; debts cause Bombay Deccan Riots 1875.

Taluqdars crushed 1801-22. Holt Mackenzie's Regulation VII of 1822 settles with the Mahal; R.M. Bird 1833 assesses 66% for 30 years; Dalhousie 48-56 extends it. Awadh summary settlement 1856 feeds 1857.
British demand cash, not grain. Moneylenders and traders push ryots from food crops to indigo, cotton, opium, jute, sugarcane for British factories. Less grain stored feeds late 19th century famines.
Cornwallis 86-93 made PS, Munro made Ryotwari, Mahalwari was a compromise. In all three, high demand, bad surveys and moneylenders left the ryot worse off than the Mughal patta.
17: Since 1765 EIC runs Civil, Military, Revenue (CMR): a Company State. Br State is anxious, yet needs its two incomes and imperial power. So from 1773 it regulates CMR.
Five worries: money (400,000 pounds a year, 1767), America lost 1783, bankruptcy and 1.4 million pounds 1772, Famine 1770 and Nabobs, Clive 57-67 and Hastings 73-85 wanting a Crown link.
Governor of Bengal becomes GG(Bengal), senior to Bombay and Madras. Supreme Council of GG + 4 decides by majority; GG has only a casting vote, a check on empire-builders.
Parliament's right to regulate EIC politics is recognised. GG reports to Directors, Directors to the State. Supreme Court at Calcutta (Elijah Impey first, 1774); no gifts for officials.

Court clashes with council; Bombay's Treaty of Surat 1775 starts the 1st Anglo-Maratha War. GG has no veto: Philip Francis blocks Hastings 73-85, Burke's impeachment ends in acquittal. Amending Act 1781.

13 colonies lost 1783, so London controls. Board of Control takes politics, Directors keep commerce: Double Government 1784-1833, Dual Control 1784-1858. Veto in 1786; Cornwallis 86-93 holds both posts.
EIC is the Crown's agent: top men appointed by EIC only with Crown approval; Parliament renews the Charter. Head belongs to the State, body to EIC. Cornwallis 86-93's Code makes law written.
Adam Smith (1776), reformers and manufacturers attack the monopoly. India trade monopoly ends (Tea, Opium, China stay); Crown sovereignty stated; missionaries enter; Rs 1 lakh a year for education.
St Helena Act: EIC stops business, stays political agent. GG(India)-in-Council (Bentinck 28-35 first); Governors lose law-making; Macaulay Law Member, Law Commission 1834; UCS opens to Indians.

Charter lasts only till Parliament decides. Civil Services exam (London, 1855) ends EIC patronage; Budget goes to Parliament; legislative council of twelve; Dalhousie 48-56 appoints Halliday first LG of Bengal 1854.
EIC blamed for 1857. GOI Act 1858: Secretary of State with 15-member India Council replaces BoC; Canning 56-62 first Viceroy; Zafar 37-57 ends; Proclamation promises; Royal Titles Act 1876.
Britain claimed no policy of conquest; EIC officials' Sub-Imperialism drove it, banned by 1784. Yet the State gave the Charter, sent troops, followed the money and used EIC as foreign-policy tool.
18: EIC turns from trader to Company State (1765-1858) and must decide how much Indian machinery to keep. Three pillars: judiciary, civil services, police. Teacher: Public Administration in British India.
Before 1772 two ladders in Bengal. Civil (Diwani): courts up to Sadar Diwani Adalat, Pandits and Maulvis. Criminal (Nizamat): Islamic law; Kazi judges, Mufti interprets, Faujdar arrests.
After Allahabad 1765 EIC holds Diwani, Nawab keeps Nizamat: Dual Government. Muhammad Reza Khan heads both; EIC cares only for revenue. Law and order breaks; Famine 1770 kills one-third of Bengal.
Hastings 73-85 ends Dual Government in 1772. DC judges civil cases; Kazi and Mufti stay in criminal courts under the DC. Supreme Court Calcutta 1774; Gentoo Code 1776, Hedaya 1791, Code of 1781.

PS 1793 makes Zamindars owners needing trusted courts; DC auctioning and judging is a conflict. Cornwallis 86-93 strips the DC of judicial power, creates four divisions, Anglo-Muhammadan law, Indians out of senior posts.

Courts clog and lawyers prolong cases. Ryotwari Madras (1814, Munro) and Bombay (1819, Elphinstone) merge DC roles again. Bentinck 28-35 ends divisional courts; Macaulay's Law Commission leads to CPC 1859, IPC 1860, CrPC 1861.

Early officials came by patronage. Cornwallis 86-93 builds Covenanted (Europeans, senior) and Uncovenanted (junior, locals) services with better pay and seniority; entry stays by nomination until Charter Act 1853.

Charter Act 1853 brings an exam, first in London 1855. Three locks: low age limit, English Literature syllabus (Brown Sahibs), London venue. Satyendranath Tagore first Indian through 1864; four more 1867.
WEMC demands exam in India; British give Lytton 76-80's lateral entry, ICS 1892 (Lansdowne 88-94), exam in India 1922, PSC 1926 (Ross Barker), Federal PSC 1937, UPSC 1950.

Mughal chain: Naib Nazim, Faujdar, Kotwal, Zamindar. Hastings 73-85 replaces Faujdars 1781. Cornwallis 86-93 ends zamindar police 1793: Indian Daroga, thanas of 30 square miles. Daroga-Zamindar nexus oppresses; Wellesley 98-05 restores zamindars 1799.

Irish Constabulary model, tested in Sindh (Charles Napier 1843), is chosen. Court's 1860 commission under Canning 56-62; Police Act March 1861 creates IG, SP, SI posts. Fraser 1902-03: Imperial Police; IPS 1948.
Each reform followed a crisis (1770 famine, 1857) or Indian movement pressure, only as far as cost or politics demanded. Legacy: codified law, organised civil service, hierarchical police.
